initial_scene: The upright humanoid faces the tabletop toward image left. A dark wired computer mouse sits near the table edge in front of the robot, with its cable lying to image left. The near-side left arm hangs beside the body; the far-side right arm is initially lowered and partly occluded. The camera shows the robot from its left side with a view toward its front.

observed_sequence.action: Robot stands beside the table with the mouse resting on it; the near-side left arm remains lowered and the active right hand has not reached the mouse.
Far-side right shoulder and elbow raise the right forearm. The open articulated right hand emerges in front of the torso and advances toward the mouse. The left arm stays down.
Right hand advances over the mouse and descends, with fingers spread and directed down toward its upper surface. The mouse remains on the tabletop.

Right fingers settle onto and around the upper mouse surface and make small downward/flexing motions while the forearm holds position. Hand partly occludes the mouse; this is consistent with button pressing but individual button travel, precise contacting digit, and registered clicks are not resolvable. No lifting or hand-to-hand transfer occurs.
Right fingers lift from the mouse. The right hand rises clear of the tabletop and the elbow bends to retract the arm toward the upper body. The mouse remains in its tabletop position.

Right hand retracts behind the visible head/torso toward a resting position and becomes partly occluded. The robot stays upright, left arm still down, and the mouse is unobstructed on the tabletop at the ending.
